summary.text: J.D. Ford is the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 5th District. A former fraternity executive and nonprofit professional, he has represented Indiana Senate District 29 since 2018 as the first openly LGBTQ+ member of the General Assembly and is not seeking re-election to the state Senate. His campaign emphasizes affordability, healthcare and care costs.

paragraphs.text: According to his Candidate Connection survey, Ford learned the value of hard work from his father, a union truck driver, and his mother, an assisted living administrator, and was influenced by grandparents who served as local officials.
He earned a bachelor's degree in political science and criminal justice from the University of Akron in 2005 and a master's degree in education from Purdue University in 2010.
He worked as senior director of recruitment and expansion for Theta Chi Fraternity, Inc., and Ballotpedia lists his profession as nonprofit professional.
Ford was elected to Indiana Senate District 29 on November 6, 2018, defeating Republican incumbent Mike Delph, and took office the next day. He was re-elected in 2022.
He describes himself as the first, and so far only, openly LGBTQ+ member of the Indiana General Assembly.

In the 2025-2026 session he serves on the Senate's Commerce and Technology, Education and Career Development, Health and Provider Services, Elections, Family & Children Services, Homeland Security and Transportation, Utilities, and Veterans Affairs and the Military committees. Earlier he served as ranking minority member of several committees and as vice chair of the Ethics Committee.
Ford won the Democratic nomination for Indiana's 5th Congressional District in the May 5, 2026 primary and faces Republican Rep. Victoria Spartz in November.
He lives in Wayne Township, Indiana.

sources.title: Gay Indiana State Sen. J.D. Ford Wins Congressional Primary
